To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the theoretical errors are larger than the experimental errors in the kinematic region where the DGLAP evolution breaks down, and smaller than the experimental errors elsewhere.
the theoretical errors are large, that the uncertainties in the data are large, that these uncertainties are correlated and that they are of similar magnitude.
the theoretical uncertainties are generally smaller than the experimental uncertainties, but in the case of W and Higgs production at the TeVatron the theoretical uncertainties dominate.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the reliability of parton distributions in the context of perturbative QCD.
the reliability of predictions from the DGLAP formalism, and with the uncertainties in the extraction of parton distributions, which are due to theoretical issues.
the question of how well we know the partons in the proton and how that knowledge can be exploited.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the theoretical uncertainties in the parton distributions are not yet well understood, but that the current theoretical uncertainties are small for the Tevatron, and for the Higgs cross sections at the LHC.

the theoretical uncertainties are large in the region of the parton distributions where the data are not fully consistent with the DGLAP approximation, but are small in the region where the data are consistent with this approximation, and hence where the NNLO prediction is a reliable guide to the accuracy to be expected in the future.
the theoretical uncertainties are not large, and that the NNLO predictions are reliable.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the theoretical errors in parton distributions can be reduced significantly by using NNLO fits to the data, but that there is still a substantial residual theoretical error which can be attributed to the breakdown of the DGLAP description at small x.

, although the theoretical uncertainties are large, the DGLAP evolution of the parton distributions is a robust description of the data, and the uncertainties in the parton distributions are dominated by those on the experimental data, rather than by those on the theory.

we have obtained a new set of NNLO partons which are conservative in the sense that the DGLAP evolution is consistent with all the data, and which have a theoretical error which is competitive with that due to the experimental uncertainties.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the uncertainties on parton distributions are now under control, and that they are small for many observables of phenomenological interest.
, in the kinematic domain where perturbative QCD is reliable, the theoretical errors are small, typically 1-2%.

, in order to obtain the best theoretical predictions from parton distribution functions, one must use a set of partons that has been determined using the most reliable theoretical framework, and which includes all the relevant theoretical corrections.
